requirement.summary: General v3 membership interface - wrongly saves coupon number and coupon name from voided set menu item into last ordered item
requirement.description:
It is available of General V3 membership interface

Vendor key: general_v3

System wrongly saved the coupon serial number and coupon name from the canceled set menu item into the last ordered item

Setup

1. Set the mapping of the external coupon code and menu item code (Set Menu item)

* Location: Interface Control > Interfaces

* Vendor: General V3 membership interface

* Section: Coupon Activation Setup

* Setup name: Coupon code mapping

> Setting the target mapping of coupon code and menu item code (Set Menu item)

2. Set the predefined child item on set menu

* Location: Menu Management > Item Properties > Set Menu

* Target set menu item

* Button "Add New"

* Add the child item into set menu

3. Allow to change item name of child item

* Location: Menu Management > Item Properties > Items

* Target child item of set menu item

* Section: Ordering Control

* Setup Name: Input Item Name

> Setting value as "Allow to change item name" or "Allow to append text after item name" or "Allow to change item name and append text after item name"

{+}Workflow

{+}1. Open new check

2. Click function "Coupon Activation" for the first coupon

3. System prompts the input box for asking coupon number

4. Input the coupon number manually or scan coupon number

5. Click button "Enter"

6. System orders the set menu parent item on ordering basket

7. System prompts the input box for appending description

8. Enter value of append description

9. Click button "OK"

10. System order the child item in set menu item

11. System prompts the input box for asking the next coupon number

12. Click button "x" to close the input box to return to ordering panel

13. The coupon number of the first set menu item is "111"

14. Click function "Coupon Activation" for the second coupon

15. System prompts the input box for asking coupon number

16. Input the coupon number manually or scan coupon number (e.g. coupon number "222"

17. Click button "Enter"

18. System orders the set menu parent item on ordering basket

19. System prompts the input box for appending description

20. Click button "Cancel"

21. System voids the current set menu item

Actual result:

System wrongly saves the coupon number and coupon name into the last item (The first set menu item). After save check, there are 2 sets of coupon number and coupon name saved in the first set menu item on database

* Coupon number :111

* Coupon number :222

Expected result:

System would not save the coupon number and coupon name of voided set menu into the last item

requirement.summary: KDS2-DEV-03-2-13: POS / KDS ticket mutation idempotency via ticket_request_idempotency
requirement.description:
Goal

When POS or KDS retries the same ticket action (network glitch, timeout, client retry), the server should recognize it as “already done” and not change the ticket again.

Clients send a request id (X-Request-Id). We save that id in ticket_request_idempotency after a successful first run. Same shop + outlet + business date + request id later = treat as a replay.

Success criteria

- Replaying the same request does not create another ticket, change items again, bump version again, write another history/event, or send MQTT again.

- Create ticket: first call creates the ticket; replay returns that same ticket.

- Other ticket updates (POS and KDS): first call does the work; replay returns success and skips the work.

- Two retries at the same time still only apply once (DB unique key helps).

- Basic unit tests cover save/lookup and “already recorded” cases.

Implementation notes

- Store one row per handled request: shop, outlet, business date, request id, and which ticket it affected.

- Shared helper: look up if we’ve seen this key; if yes, skip; if no, do the work then save the key in the same DB transaction.

- Create ticket is special: on replay, load and return the original ticket from the saved row.

- Request id only needs to be unique within that shop/outlet/business date—not worldwide.

- Don’t run side effects (MQTT, events, version bump) on a replay.

# <<< [Not Included In STD Release] >>>
New Functions: [JIRA-60479] POS / KDS ticket mutation idempotency via ticket_request_idempotency
Descriptions:
When POS or KDS retries the same ticket action (network glitch, timeout, client retry), the server should recognize it as “already done” and not change the ticket again.
Clients send a request id (X-Request-Id). We save that id in ticket_request_idempotency after a successful first run. Same shop + outlet + business date + request id later = treat as a replay.
Setup:
POS / KDS will retry same ticket action, for example, addTicket. For each API, POS / KDS can self-define the X-Request-Id which is max. 26-character long in the HTTP header. This X-Request-Id is to identify each request and recognize if the request has “done” before and do not change the ticket again.
If the request replays with same X-Request-Id, for example, addTicket, no duplicated ticket will be created on KDS if multiple request with same X-Request-Id sent from POS.
POS / KDS ticket mutation idempotency is supported for all KDS & POS APIs.

requirement.release_notes:
# Enhancement: [HERO-69066] [Tech] TMS 2.0 - Function Authority control in Backend API - Dev - 2/2 + Testing
# Desciption:
# This case focuses on strengthening the security checking of API callings. Functions are now required to be involved in authority checking in both Frontend and called externally. Function keys are relatively referring in TMS Function Authority, and functions in Operation mode will be controlled by those.
# Setup:
# 1. Setup
Mode A login: a shop user (not admin/system) who has authorities (Allow) on the function under test.
Mode B login: a shop user who has no authorities (Deny / no Allow row) on that function. For Ask Authority, a second user who has Allow is required.
Outlet under test: Infrasys Restaurant (outlet_id 1). Relogin or refetch GET function_authorities after changing Set Function Authorities.
## 1.1 Mode A — Allow + Ask Password + Ask Approval
Set Function Authorities: Allow the logged-in user on the function, tick Ask Password and Ask Approval. GET function_authorities returns ask_password,ask_approval. UI: password of the logged-in user (who has authorities), then login and password of another user who also has Allow.
Figure 1. Authority : Ask Password — Password only. Enter the logged-in user's password, Submit.
Figure 2. Authority : Ask Approval — Login name and password of a user who has authorities, Submit.
## 1.2 Mode B — Deny + Ask Authority
Set Function Authorities: the logged-in user has no authorities (Deny), tick Ask Authority. GET returns ask_authority. UI shows Login Name + Password for a user who has Allow. Do not use the logged-in (no-authority) user's own password.
Figure 3. Authority : Ask Authority (logged in as a user who has no authorities). Login Name and Password of a user who has Allow.
## 1.3 Shared expected sequence (Mode A)
1) Trigger the function (see each case). 2) Figure 1 — Ask Password. 3) Figure 2 — Ask Approval. 4) Action continues. Cancel at any dialog must not run the action.
# 2. Succeeded function cases
## 2.1 Current View (enter)
Function key: current_view
Steps:
1. Log in Operation as a shop user who has Allow on the function (Mode A) or who has no Allow / Deny (Mode B). Do not use admin or system.
2. Open navbar Current View, or go to the URL above (first enter or after outlet change).
3. Mode A: dialog Authority : Ask Password (Password only). Enter the logged-in user's password → Submit.
4. Then dialog Authority : Ask Approval. Enter login name and password of another user who has Allow on the same function → Submit.
5. Mode B (user has no authorities + Ask Authority): Authority : Ask Authority with Login Name + Password of a user who has Allow. Do not use the logged-in user's own password.
Mode A result: Pass (17 Sep live, login 6): Ask Password (password 6) then Ask Approval (login 1 / password 1), then floor plan loads. Session Welcome, 6.
Mode B result: Pass — Ask Authority on first enter.

Ask Approval after password (same sequence for every Mode A case).

Where: .../tms/operation/calendar_view
Steps:

2. Same dual dialogs as Current View (Mode A) or Ask Authority (Mode B).
Mode A result: Pass (17 Sep live): Ask Password (6) then Ask Approval (1 / 1), calendar floor plan loads.
Mode B result: Pass — Ask Authority on enter.
Screenshot for Calendar View (enter).
## 2.3 Walk In

2. Click Walk In.

Mode A result: Pass (17 Sep live): Walk In → Ask Password (6) → Ask Approval (1 / 1) → booking panel (Auto Assign Table / Special Remarks).
Mode B result: Pass — Ask Authority on Walk In.
